ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY COUNCIL The City Council may discuss and act upon items described under Council Comments; however, items which are not will be limited to Council reports, announcements, or requests for clarification, or factual information, or to placement of matters on the agenda for a future meeting.
6.
ORAL COMMUNICATIONS Persons wishing to speak on Consent Agenda items or subjects other than those scheduled are requested to do so at this time. When addressing the Council, please come to the podium and give your name and address for the record. In order to conduct a timely meeting, a 5 minute time limit per person has been established. Amendments to Government Code Section 54954.2 prohibit the Council from taking action or engaging in discussion on a specific item unless it appears on a posted agenda.
7.

minutes_text:
MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE LOMITA CITY COUNCIL
  October 1, 2012

1. OPENING CEREMONIES

  a. Call Meeting to Order

A regular meeting of the Lomita City Council was called to order at 7 p.m. on Monday, October
1, 2012, in the Council Chambers, Lomita City Hall, 24300 Narbonne Avenue.

  b. Flag Salute

Mayor Gazeley led the salute to the flag.

  c. Invocation

Councilmember Sanchez gave the invocation.

  d. Roll Call

Those responding to roll call by Assistant City Clerk Shumway were COUNCILMEMBERS:
Estrada, Sanchez, Savidan, Traina, and Mayor Gazeley. Also present were City Manager Rock,
Assistant City Manager Sugano, Administrative Services Director Chavez, City Attorney Hogin,
Community Services Director McPherron, Public Works Director Damasse, Parks and
Recreation Director Harding, and Assistant City Clerk Shumway.

2.  PRESENTATIONS

Mayor Gazeley announced the resignation of Public Safety and Traffic Commissioner
Jankowski, and in lieu of a service plaque, Mr. Jankowski requested that the money be donated
to Community Child. Mayor Gazeley and City Councilmembers presented a check to Tara
Nierenhausen, Community Child's Executive Director.

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the agenda. Councilmember Savidan seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

4.  CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

City Manager Rock introduced the City of Lomita's new Parks and Recreation Director, Mr.
Cameron Harding. Director Harding stated that he is looking forward to working with staff and
the City Council.

City Manager Rock announced that the agenda item pertaining to placing recycling containers at
the City's parks will be brought back to the City Council on October 15, 2012, and that the public

  Page 1 of 5
 hearing regarding the City of Lomita's Capital Improvement Projects has been scheduled for
November 5, 2012.

City Manager Rock also reminded everyone that City Hall would be closed on October 8, 2012,
for Columbus Day.

City Manager Rock informed the City Council that the recommendations from the Public Safety
and Traffic Commission, regarding the crosswalk near the intersection of Lomita Boulevard and
Narbonne Avenue, will be brought back to the City Council for discussion once they complete its
review.

City Manager Rock reported that the broken street lights pointed out by Councilmember Traina
during the previous City Council meeting had been repaired. City Manager Rock asked City
Councilmembers if they would be interested in the formation of a Finance Committee, which
would consist of the Mayor, Mayor Pro Tem, the City Manager, and the Administrative Services
Director. According to City Manager Rock, the purpose of the Finance Committee would be to
review various finance issues, including the preparation of the annual budget, the purchasing
cards policy, the reserve fund policy, the investment policy, etc. Councilmember Traina moved
to direct staff to bring back to City Council a resolution for the formation of a Finance Committee.
Councilmember Savidan seconded the motion, which carried unanimously.

City Manager Rock concluded his report by stating that the City Council retreat will be held in
late January or early February 2013, and that City Councilmembers need to finalize a date for
the retreat.

5.  ORAL COMMUNICATIONS AND MEETING ATTENDANCE REPORTS FROM THE CITY
  COUNCIL

Councilmember Sanchez reported that he and Mayor Gazeley attended a Contract Cities event
at Los Angeles County Fire Station 110. According to Councilmember Sanchez, based on the
equipment that they saw at Fire Station 110, Los Angeles County Fire is well prepared for any
disaster.

Councilmember Savidan asked that the City Council revisit the discussion of a dog park within
the City of Lomita, which City Council voted to agendize for a future meeting during the City
Council Meeting held on September 17, 2012. According to Councilmember Savidan, he can no
longer support this future agenda item due to the fact that it would be not fiscally responsible for
the City, and that there are more pressing issues that require immediate attention from staff and
the City Council. Councilmember Savidan moved to rescind the vote of September 17, 2012,
which requested the placement of the dog park discussion on a future agenda. Mayor Gazeley
seconded the motion.

Councilmember Traina stated that this item was for discussion only and he felt it should be
placed on a future agenda, as City Council Meeting agendas have been relatively short, and
residents should be able to bring forward issues and discuss them in a public forum.

ROLL CALL:
Ayes: Councilmembers Estrada, Savidan, and Mayor Gazeley
Noes: Councilmembers Traina and Sanchez

  Page 2 of 5
 Councilmember Traina stated that he attended Cindy Blount’s retirement party and wanted to
again thank Ms. Blount for her service to the City and her dedication to the kids, parks, and the
City. Councilmember Traina also reported that he met with City Manager Rock and
Councilmember Sanchez regarding the salary allocations to the Water Enterprise Fund, which
Councilmember Traina described as very productive, with most of his questions being
answered. Councilmember Traina requested that City Manager Rock provide feedback
regarding some of the outstanding questions and actions that came up during their meeting.
Furthermore, Councilmember Traina stated that it is very important that the costs charged to the
Water Enterprise Fund are true and reasonable so that rates charged to water rate payers are
fair.

Mayor Gazeley reported that on September 21, 2012, he, along with Councilmembers Estrada
and Savidan, attended a ceremony and plaque dedication for Tim King at the LA County
Sheriff’s Harbor Division, which was in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the crisis response
team that Captain King started over 20 years ago.

6. ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

Pearl Georgen, Lomita resident, stated that she received a notice from her landlord regarding an
upcoming $30 monthly parking charge at her residence. Ms. Georgen asked if the City could
assist her in this matter, as parking on the street is congested and could be potentially unsafe
for residents.

George Kivett, Executive Director of the Lomita Chamber of Commerce, thanked City staff and
the Railroad Museum Foundation for hosting the latest business mixer, and announced that
everyone was invited to attend the next business mixer, which will be at Optometric Concierge
on October 25, 2012. Mr. Kivett also announced the upcoming grand reopening of Home Health
Depot, which will take place on October 11, 2012, as well as the opening of Grandmas’
Catering, which is planned for October 17, 2012. Furthermore, Mr. Kivett recommended that in
the future the City needs to send City staff to the International Conference of Shopping Centers
(ICSC), which could be very beneficial in terms of bringing businesses to Lomita.

George Kivett, Lomita resident, asked that City staff follow-up on curbs scraped by the street
sweeper at 241st Street, between Walnut and Eshelman. Mr. Kivett also stated that he was in
agreement with Councilmember Traina that residents should be allowed to request agenda
items and discuss matters in this public forum.

City Manager Rock noted that City staff would follow-up on the scraped curb issue, and added
that Charles Felix, Special Project Coordinator, attended the ICSC Conference in San Diego on
September 20, 2012.

7. CONSENT AGENDA

Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the consent agenda. Councilmember Sanchez
seconded the motion. Councilmember Traina asked to pull Item 7.I for discussion. The motion
carried unanimously.

  Page 3 of 5
 In regards to Item 7.I, Councilmember Traina asked why there was such a big difference
between the two bids in terms of cost proposal. Public Works Director Damasse responded that
while both companies are well qualified to perform the work, WQTS has higher staff cost rates
and included additional tests and work in their proposal, all of which significantly increased their
proposal amount. Director Damasse added that the work to be performed was very specialized
and that it is very difficult to find consultants in this area. Director Damasse further stated that
even if WQTS reduced some of the additional tests and work, their cost proposal would still be
much higher than Hazen and Sawyer, P.C., which staff has recommended.

Councilmember Traina moved to approve Item 7.I.  Councilmember Estrada seconded the
motion, which carried unanimously.

  a. Motion to Waive Further Reading.

  b. Recommendation to approve the minutes for the City Council Meeting held on September
  17, 2012. RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  c. Approval of Demands.

  d. Report dealing with economic development activities. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  e. Report dealing with activities of the Parks and Recreation Department. RECEIVE AND
  FILE.

  f. Report dealing with activities of the Public Works Department. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  g. Report presenting the Treasurer’s Report. RECEIVE AND FILE.

  h. Report submitting the City of Lomita's 2012 Conflict of Interest Code Biennial Notice.
  RECEIVE AND FILE.

  i.  Report submitting approval of a Professional Services Agreement for Offline Testing at
  the Cypress Water Production Facility with Hazen and Sawyer (Consultant) in an amount
  not to exceed $29,892, and establish a total project budget of $34,376 (including 15%
  contingency.) RECOMMEND APPROVAL.

  PUBLIC HEARING

8.  Citizens Option for Public Safety

Community Service Director McPherron stated that City receives $100,000 for the COPS
program, which appropriates money to fund front line staff (CORE Deputy position). Director
McPherron recommended approval of the resolution.

Mayor Gazeley opened public input. There were none.

  Page 4 of 5
 Councilmember Estrada moved to approve the resolution for the COPS program, as
recommended by staff.  Councilmember Traina seconded the motion, which carried
unanimously.

ADJOURNMENT

Meeting adjourned at 7:44 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,

__________________________________
Lena Shumway, Assistant City Clerk, CMC
